To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

XML-based NLP toolkits are very flexible and that they can be used in combination with a wide range of other NLP tools, both XML-based and non-XML-based, to create a highly effective system for the analysis of medical language.

XML-based tools and the integration of off-the-shelf tools have proved to be very useful in the development of a corpus of MEDLINE documents that has been annotated with information about the medical domain.
XML NLP tools can be used to produce a highly accurate corpus of medical language and that the annotations in this corpus have been used to enhance the performance of two NLP tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of NLP tools and techniques for processing medical language.
the use of XML mark-up to facilitate the integration of NLP tools and to provide a common representation for the results of the analysis.

the development of a suite of XML-based NLP processing tools for the analysis and annotation of medical texts, which are being used to create a corpus of annotated MEDLINE abstracts, and the use of the corpus in a number of NLP research tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how XML-based tools and mark-up can play a key part in the development of NLP tools for processing and analysing the language of the medical domain.
the use of XML mark-up and the XML tools has been a major factor in enabling us to achieve our goals.
the use of XML mark-up has made the analysis process more flexible and more transparent, and the annotated corpus is of high quality and can be used for many purposes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XML mark-up has played a key role in the analysis process.
the integration of XML tools has enabled us to create a highly annotated corpus that is a rich source of information for a range of applications.
the use of XML-based mark-up and XML-based tools has been a major factor in enabling us to build the tools and pipelines needed to analyse medical text.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of highly flexible and configurable XML tools, together with more traditional 'hand-crafted' tools, can be used effectively to produce annotated corpora for use in a variety of applications.
XML-based NLP is an excellent approach to the analysis of text in any domain where a rich set of annotations is required.
XML mark-up is an essential component of the NLP pipeline for medical text.
